headline: Chinese AI chip maker Iluvatar CoreX has unveiled a rack-sized computer that links 144 of its GPUs, which it says is the densest of its kind and cuts the cost of generating AI output by 40%.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the system was unveiled on 12 Oct, before the window, and the claims are the company's own.
importance_line: It shows Chinese chipmakers building rack-scale systems to rival Nvidia's, which matters to Chinese AI developers short of top US chips, but the density and 40% cost claims are the company's own and the speed of its chips is not stated.
summary: BigGo Finance reports that Iluvatar CoreX, a Hong Kong-listed Chinese maker of AI chips, unveiled the Tiangai 300 IXL144 on 12 Oct 2026 at the China International Industry Fair, a "supernode" (a group of chips wired to work like one big computer) that packs 144 GPUs, 18 CPUs and about 10.1 terabytes of video memory into one standard rack. The company calls it the highest-density system of its kind and says it lowers the cost per million effective tokens by 40% against mainstream international products, a claim for which BigGo reports no outside test.
notes: Event dated 12 Oct (before the window), so the score is lowered by 1 as instructed. SCMP, the pool item, was blocked; BigGo Finance is credited because its text was read.
